clue.text: Depressed after drug blitz

indicators.note: after places the word for depressed behind the drug in the answer

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
feeling depressed is feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone feeling low after a narcotics raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz is a sudden concerted campaign of enforcement, as police mount against crime.

clue.text: Angry at wrong mark

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at being given a mistaken grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyed people are described as being in a bad temper this way, and a wrong answer on a test is marked with an X.

clue.text: Real gold — and afterwards endless credit

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
then means afterwards, next

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the credit word is dropped

parts.note: buying on tick means buying on credit

explanation.surface: A claim that the gold is genuine, followed by unlimited borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something genuine, not fake, is real.

clue.text: Knight waves his finger at the flier

parts.note: K is the chess notation for king; N for knight, but K is also an abbreviation for knight as in KBE

indicators.note: waves suggests the letters of his finger being waved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A knight gestures threateningly at a passing bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' is a bird, not a pilot or a leaflet; the threatening gesture is the anagram signal 'waves'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird is a creature that flies, and this colourful riverside bird is one.

clue.text: Reveals the Scottish flower can last longer

parts.note: outs means reveals, as in outing a secret
the Tay is a Scottish river, a 'flower' because it flows

explanation.surface: A Scottish bloom that is shown off lasts well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' here means something that flows, a river: the TAY runs through Perth in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain somewhere beyond the expected time is to last longer there.

clue.text: Fail to support first nominee, then vote to include German

indicators.note: first picks only the opening letter of nominee
to include signals the German letter going inside the voting word

parts.note: to elect is to vote in

explanation.surface: Advice to choose a candidate first and include a German in the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts G inside ELECT, giving EGLECT after N.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something uncared for is to fail to look after or support it.

clue.text: Note on college is not true

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
the LSE is the London School of Economics, a college

explanation.surface: A remark about a university that is untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is incorrect or wrong.

clue.text: After losing right to organise the lot

indicators.note: organise means the remaining letters are arranged into a new order
losing means the letter for right is taken away from after

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to arrange everything having lost their privileges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes R out of AFTER, leaving AFTE, which 'to organise' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny.

clue.text: Free toilets? Ecstasy!

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Free public lavatories prompt delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfastened or released from restraint is free.

clue.text: Businessman can cut off about four

indicators.note: about means the execution word goes around the numeral

parts.note: to execute someone is to cut off their life, as by beheading
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A trader is able to reduce a figure by roughly four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' means to kill, as in beheading; 'about' signals the container and 'can' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior manager in a company is a business person.

clue.text: Catch the diplomats coming back on many occasions

indicators.note: coming back turns the catching word and the diplomats round together

parts.note: to net something is to catch it
the FO, the Foreign Office, is Britain's diplomatic service

explanation.surface: Ambassadors returning home are frequently caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses NETFO to give OFTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens frequently happens repeatedly.

clue.text: Where the circus performer treads carefully to grip the roundabout

definitions.text: Where the circus performer treads carefully

indicators.note: roundabout suggests the letters of to grip the going round into a new order

explanation.surface: An acrobat steps gingerly to keep hold on a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like the fairground ride but rearranges TO GRIP THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-wire walker balances on a taut cable stretched above the ring.

clue.text: Relative needs guide to get round fellow in the way

indicators.note: to get round means the guide word encloses the rest

parts.note: to steer is to guide

indicators.note: in places the fellow letter inside the way

parts.note: a path is a way

explanation.surface: A relation needs someone to lead them around a man blocking the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'in' puts the fellow into the way, and 'to get round' wraps the guide around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother's husband who is not one's father is a family member by marriage.

clue.text: Statesmen use a hidden agenda

indicators.note: hidden says the letters lie concealed inside statesmen use

explanation.surface: Politicians operate with a secret plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with, such as a programme of business, is an agenda.

clue.text: Nonsense, painting one disorderly bar upsets judge

indicators.note: upsets turns the whole string of pieces upside down, which in a down clue reverses it

parts.note: rot means nonsense
painting is art
I is one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: disorderly means the letters of bar are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rowdy pub scene with dreadful artwork offends a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' turns BAR into BRA; 'upsets' then reverses ROTARTIBRA to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appointed to settle a dispute acts as its judge.

clue.text: Please say it's somehow loud inside

indicators.note: inside places the loud letter within the rearranged letters
somehow means the letters of say it's are rearranged in some fashion

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A polite request delivered with a raised voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges SAY ITS into SATISY, and 'inside' slots F in.
explanation.definitionFit: To gratify or content someone is to please them.

clue.text: Disreputable person caught accomplice with fruits of crime outside

indicators.note: outside means the loot word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: swag is stolen loot
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ally is a partner or accomplice

explanation.surface: A crook is arrested with a partner, surrounded by stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or rogue is a disreputable sort.

clue.text: The ends of lines

parts.note: read as railway lines or bus routes, the stations at the far ends of each route

explanation.definitionFit: Stations at the end of a railway or bus route are its terminal points.

clue.text: Concentrated on organising the seven in it

indicators.note: organising means the letters of seven in it are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Focused on getting the seven people within into order.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly concentrated effort or study is thorough and intense.

clue.text: A collection of books, including nice assortment from early times

indicators.note: including means the testament letters go around the jumbled letters

parts.note: the NT, New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

indicators.note: assortment means the letters of nice are mixed up

explanation.surface: A library containing a pleasant mix of very old volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment' jumbles nice, and 'including' sets that inside the New Testament abbreviation; 'books' suggests a library, not scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dating from long ago is old or antique.

clue.text: Paper with hit over broken idol

indicators.note: over turns the hitting word upside down, reversing it in a down clue

parts.note: to bat is to hit

indicators.note: broken means the letters of idol are jumbled

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about striking a shattered statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns BAT into TAB; 'broken' rearranges IDOL into LOID.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular, sensational newspaper is a kind of paper.

clue.text: Take umbrage at facial hair

explanation.surface: Someone offended by another's beard.
explanation.definitionFit: To show irritation or offence is to bridle, and a short stiff hair on the face is a stubble hair.

clue.text: They can get fairly distressed at the hairdressers

definitions.text: They can get fairly distressed at the hairdressers

parts.words: They can get fairly distressed at the hairdressers
parts.note: fairly means with fair hair, and distressed hints at tresses being treated in the salon

explanation.definitionFit: Fair-haired women may have their light-coloured hair styled or bleached at a salon.

clue.text: Allows for things getting in the way

explanation.surface: Permission given for obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Permits means allows, and in tennis a serve clipping the net must be replayed, just as 'without let or hindrance' means without obstruction.

clue.text: Brave Pole

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and the clue reads as the carved post such peoples erect

explanation.definitionFit: A carved, painted pole set up by Native American peoples bears an emblem of a clan.

clue.text: Loathing the sailor — he turns corner inside

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: inside places the jumbled letters within he
turns means the letters of corner are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor despises the job of steering round a sharp bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' is the pronoun taken as written; 'turns' jumbles corner and 'inside' sets it within those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense hatred or disgust is loathing.

clue.text: For example, hit out at the crew

indicators.note: out signals the letters being knocked into a new order

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An example of a strike at the rowing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EG plus HIT. A rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, a boat of eight oarsmen is the crew itself.

clue.text: Closed the second building

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a hut is a simple building

explanation.surface: The second building has been closed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is closed is not open.

clue.text: Perhaps Albert has some thing to say for the slogan

parts.note: an Albert is a watch chain named after Prince Albert, so suggests a timepiece
a word is something you say

explanation.surface: Prince Albert has a motto to proclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: An Albert is a style of chain for a pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto or rallying cry is a slogan.

clue.text: Skinny girl starts to object

parts.note: skinny means thin

indicators.note: starts picks the opening letter of girl

explanation.surface: A slim young woman begins to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: An article or item is an object.

clue.text: Scale of turnover at unionists journal

indicators.note: of turnover means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: TU, trade union, stands for unionists
a mag, magazine, is a journal

explanation.surface: Sales figures at a trade union magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The full range of something, as of musical notes, is its scale.

clue.text: Confuse with muddled directions — caught out

indicators.note: muddled means the remaining letters are mixed up
out means the caught letter is removed from directions

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Garbled instructions leave a batsman dismissed and bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes C from DIRECTIONS, leaving DIRETIONS, which 'muddled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone lose their bearings is to bewilder them.
